title: Instrumentation and control: measure, compare, act
hook: In many designs, cut one wire to a diesel generator's oil pressure trip and the engine stops, though the oil pressure is fine. Is that a fault in the design, or the whole point of it?
oneBreath: A plant keeps itself in line by measuring, comparing what it finds with what it should be, and acting. Sensors turn temperature, pressure, level and flow into an electrical signal, often a current sent round a two-wire loop, and instruments are checked against a standard and, where needed, set again. Controllers, from a thermostat to PID and the logic in a PLC, decide what to do, and alarms and trips guard the plant, usually wired so that a broken wire or a lost supply fails safe.

ideas.title: The measurement chain: from the plant to a number
ideas.oneLine: Calibration checks an instrument's straight input-to-output line against a standard: the zero adjustment shifts the whole line, and the span adjustment tilts it.

ideas.title: Temperature: the PT100 and the thermocouple
ideas.oneLine: Both temperature sensors can be fooled by their wiring: a PT100's leads add resistance, and a thermocouple reads its hot end against its cold end.

ideas.title: Pressure, level and flow
ideas.oneLine: Pressure gives level, from the pressure at a tank's foot, and flow, from the drop across a pipe's narrowing, which grows as flow squared.

ideas.title: The 4-20 mA loop
ideas.oneLine: A 4-20 mA loop is one series ring, so the same current carries the reading over any cable length the supply can drive.

ideas.title: Control loops: measure, compare, act
ideas.oneLine: A controller compares the measured value with the set point and acts; on/off control always swings, and swings further when the reading arrives late.

ideas.title: PID: tuning a loop by feel
ideas.oneLine: A PID controller acts on the error: proportional alone leaves an offset, integral removes it but can swing, derivative damps swings but amplifies noise.

ideas.title: Logic and PLCs: from relays to ladder
ideas.oneLine: A PLC solves relay logic as a ladder, scanning over and over: read every input, solve the rungs top to bottom, then write every output.

ideas.title: Alarms, trips and fail-safe design
ideas.oneLine: A trip circuit kept energised trips on a broken wire, and sensor voting trades missed trips against false ones; designers judge which failure matters more.

calibration.q: A pressure gauge is accurate to plus or minus 1% of its whole 0 to 10 bar range. It reads 1 bar. How far out could that reading be?
calibration.why: The 1% is of the whole 10 bar range, so it allows 0.1 bar anywhere on the scale. At 1 bar that is a tenth of the reading. Taking 1% of the reading itself gives 0.01 bar, ten times too hopeful.

calibration.q: A level gauge set up on a water tank is moved to an identical tank holding oil, lighter than water, to the same depth. What will it show?
options: A greater depth than the real one
A smaller depth than the real one
calibration.why: The gauge feels the weight of liquid above it. Lighter oil at the same depth presses less, so a gauge set for water reads low. It does not read the same, because it never sees the surface, only the pressure at the bottom.
